name: Feature from a card
description: A card moved to To do goes to a builder; you approve the result before the card moves to Review.

config.brief: Implement the card's request on a branch, with tests. Keep the change small and say what you changed.

name: Bug: reproduce, then fix
description: A reproducer confirms the bug first; only a confirmed bug goes to the builder, and a gate checks the fix.

name: Nightly regression
description: Every night the test fixer runs the test suite; failing tests are fixed on a branch and opened as a draft pull request.

config.brief: Run the project's test suite. If tests fail, fix them on a branch with the smallest change and prove it.

name: Dependency hygiene
description: Weekly, a builder upgrades Go modules and another JavaScript packages; you approve both.

config.brief: Upgrade the Go modules in go.mod and go.sum to their latest patch and minor versions. Run go build and go test. Write upgrades.json listing each module, its old and new version.
Upgrade the packages in package.json and the lockfile to their latest patch and minor versions. Run the build and the tests. Write upgrades.json listing each package, its old and new version.

name: Session follow-up
description: When a session ends, a reviewer looks at what it did and posts a notice.

config.brief: Review the changes the session that just ended made. List problems with file and line, and say whether it is ready.

name: Kanban triage autopilot
description: A card entering Triage is scouted; you decide whether it goes to the backlog.

name: Friday delivery sweep
description: Every Friday a delivery crew gathers what shipped this week and you get a summary.

name: Pull request reviewer
description: A pull request opened on GitHub (not a draft) gets a review from the PR reviewer, posted as a review. Needs GitHub connected.

name: CI failure fixer
description: A failing check suite on a pull request gets the bug crew: reproduce, fix, review, then a draft pull request. Needs GitHub connected.

config.brief: The pull request's checks failed. Reproduce the failure, fix it with the smallest change and prove it with the failing check.

name: Dependabot triage
description: A Dependabot pull request gets a strategy check: is the upgrade safe, does it need code changes. The verdict is posted as a comment. Needs GitHub connected.

name: UI polish pass
description: The UI crew designs a polish pass, you approve the design, then it is built and opened as a draft pull request.

config.brief: Find the rough edges in the user interface (spacing, contrast, states, copy) and fix the worst ones.

name: Security patch train
description: Every week the security crew scans for known vulnerabilities, patches them and verifies each fix; green checks gate a draft pull request.

name: Release provenance
description: The release steward checks a release: changelog, signed tags, SBOM and provenance, and files a ticket with what is missing.

config.brief: Check the latest release: changelog, signed tag, SBOM and build provenance. List what is missing.

name: Nightly blackbox regression
description: Treats a running build as a black box: the reproducer drives it through scripted scenarios without reading source, the verifier compares with the last good run, and a decision says whether a difference is a regression. A regression becomes an issue.

config.brief: Treat the running build as a black box and do not read its source. Drive it through scripted scenarios, one for each behaviour a user can see, and record what every scenario did in run.json.

nodes.title: Compare to the last good run

config.brief: Compare run.json with the last good run and list every difference in diff.json. Report the differences only. Whether a difference is a regression is decided in the next step.

name: Feature from issue
description: An issue labelled belai:feature goes to the planner. You sign the plan off, the builder implements it, the reviewer checks it against the acceptance criteria, and a draft pull request opens.

config.brief: Read the issue and write a plan with acceptance criteria, in plan.md.
Implement the approved plan on a branch. Keep to the acceptance criteria.
Review the branch against the acceptance criteria in the plan and write review.json.

name: Malware response
description: A Dependabot alert that names malware pins the safe version, a decision sizes the blast radius, wide cases notify you, and an issue tracks the response. No model chooses whether to block.

config.brief: Pin the package named in the alert to the newest earlier version that is not flagged. Change the version pin and its lockfile entry and nothing else, and do not run install scripts from the flagged package. Record the package, the old version and the pinned version in pin.json.

config.question: How widely is the malicious package used?

name: Secret leak response
description: A secret scanning alert opens a rotation task when the secret is still live. The owner confirms the rotation.

name: Failure explainer comment
description: When checks fail on a pull request, the explainer reads the failed step and comments with the step, the lines that matter and the likely cause.

nodes.title: Checks finished on a pull request

config.brief: Read the failed check step. Write one comment with the step, the lines that matter and the likely cause.

name: Flaky test card
description: When a check fails, the flaky hunter compares it with the same check at the same commit. A test that flips gets the workflow's flaky-tests card on the board; nothing is skipped or quarantined without the sf:quarantine label.

nodes.title: Look for flips at the same commit

config.brief: Re-run the failing checks against the same commit and decide whether the failure flips. Name each flaky test.

name: Default branch broke
description: When a workflow run fails on the default branch, belai:bug finds the commit that broke it and opens a draft revert. Nothing merges.

nodes.title: Find the commit that broke it

config.brief: The default branch failed its workflow run. Find the commit that broke it and prepare a revert. Do not merge.

name: Sign build artifacts into TEA
description: When a workflow run succeeds on the default branch, the publisher matches the artifacts TEA accepts and records their digests, and the Vulnetix CLI publishes them to TEA with the run as provenance, private by default. Publishing needs the repository at draft_pr autonomy.

nodes.title: Match, sign and record the artifacts

config.brief: Match the run's artifacts, sign every one that can be signed and record the run as provenance.

name: SBOM to TEA
description: After a push to the default branch that changes dependencies, the publisher builds or picks up the CycloneDX SBOM for the new commit, and the Vulnetix CLI publishes it to TEA against the component, private by default. Publishing needs the repository at draft_pr autonomy.

nodes.title: Build or pick up the SBOM

config.brief: Build or pick up the CycloneDX SBOM for the new commit and record it against the component.

name: Low quality PR comment
description: When a person opens a pull request, the steward checks it against your contributing rules: description, linked issue, tests, size and title. It posts one specific comment. Bots and drafts are skipped.

nodes.title: Pull request opened by a person
Check the pull request against the rules

config.brief: Check the pull request against the repository's contributing rules and report only what is specifically wrong.

name: Dependabot strategy check
description: Checks a bot dependency pull request against how the repository resolves: package manager, lockfile and version range policy. A mismatch gets a corrected draft pull request.

nodes.title: Dependency pull request from a bot
Compare the bump with the strategy

config.brief: Compare the bump with how the repository resolves dependencies. If it does not match, prepare a corrected change.

name: Test dependency declared as runtime
description: Finds a dependency imported only from test, build or tooling paths but declared for runtime, and opens a draft pull request moving it to the development scope.

nodes.title: Dependency pull request from a bot
Check the scope against the imports

config.brief: Check where the dependency is imported. If only test, build or tooling paths import it, move it to the development scope and list the importers as evidence.

nodes.title: Draft pull request moving the dependency

name: Actions workflow hardening
description: Reviews pull requests that change GitHub Actions workflows: unpinned actions, broad permissions, pull_request_target with a head checkout, script injection. It comments with suggestions and never approves.

nodes.title: Workflow change in a pull request

config.brief: Review only the changed workflow files for unpinned actions, broad permissions, pull_request_target with a head checkout and script injection. Suggest changes. Never approve.

name: Issue to ticket
description: When someone on the team opens an issue, the ticket writer posts the ticket on it: user story, context, success criteria, definition of done, todos and what is out of scope. It asks for what it cannot find.

config.brief: Write the ticket in the ticket standard. Ask on the issue for anything you cannot find.

nodes.title: Post the ticket on the issue

name: Secret alert: fixture or real
description: When secret scanning raises an alert, the triager decides whether it is a test fixture or a real secret, proposes the dismissal or files a rotation issue. A secret GitHub reports as valid is never dismissed.

config.brief: Decide whether the secret is a test fixture or documented example. Propose the dismissal with a reason, or describe the rotation for a real secret. Never dismiss one GitHub reports as valid.

name: Dependabot alert triage
description: When Dependabot raises an alert, the triager checks reachability, scope, CISA KEV and EPSS, drafts a not_affected statement when no call path exists, or files an urgent issue when it is exploited.

config.brief: Check reachability, scope, CISA KEV and EPSS. Draft a VEX not_affected statement when no call path exists, or say the vulnerability is exploited.

name: Code scanning alert triage
description: When a code scanning tool raises a high or critical alert, the triager decides whether it is test code, dead code or reachable, and files an issue or proposes the dismissal with a reason.

config.brief: Decide whether the alert is in test code, dead code or reachable code. Propose a dismissal with a reason or describe the fix.

name: Release steward
description: When a release is published, the steward writes the notes from merged pull requests, checks the assets are signed and lists the downstream bumps.

config.brief: Write the release notes from the merged pull requests, check the assets are signed and list the downstream bumps.

name: Repository onboarding
description: When a repository is added, the onboarder profiles it and opens one draft pull request with a missing SECURITY.md, CODEOWNERS or dependabot.yml. It never changes branch protection.

nodes.title: Profile and set up the repository

config.brief: Profile the repository: languages, package managers, test runners and CI. Add only a missing SECURITY.md, CODEOWNERS or dependabot.yml. Never change branch protection.

nodes.title: Draft pull request with the missing files

name: Label sf:fix-tests
description: When someone adds sf:fix-tests to a pull request, the test fixer runs the failing checks and pushes the fixes as a draft pull request stacked on it.

config.brief: Run the failing checks and fix them with the smallest change.

name: Label sf:repro
description: When someone adds sf:repro to an issue, the reproducer reproduces the bug and comments the failing test on the issue.

config.brief: Reproduce the bug with a failing test and describe how to run it.

name: Label sf:review
description: When someone adds sf:review to a pull request, even a draft, the reviewer reviews it now and comments. It never approves.

config.brief: Review the pull request and comment. Never approve.

name: Investigate a risky GitHub event
description: When the organisation's audit log shows a risky change (two-factor off, protection removed or bypassed, visibility changed, a repository deleted or transferred, an app or webhook added), the investigator reads the facts and the mirror and files a ticket that says expected, needs an owner, or incident. It never changes GitHub.

config.brief: Read the event's facts (rule, action, actor, repository) and the mirror. Say whether it is expected, needs an owner, or is an incident, and why. Do not change GitHub.

name: Ticket a GitHub settings fix
description: When a repository setting gets weaker (made public, secret scanning or push protection off, default branch protection removed), the ticket writer files one ticket for the person who can change it: the setting, its current and recommended value, where it lives on GitHub and why. Nothing changes the setting itself.

config.brief: The finding is a GitHub repository or organisation setting. Write one ticket in the ticket standard: the setting, its current and recommended value, the GitHub settings page it lives on, and the abuse it allows. Do not change the setting or open a pull request.

name: Container published to TEA
description: When a container image is published to GitHub Packages, the publisher records its digest and SBOM, and the Vulnetix CLI publishes it to TEA, private by default. Publishing needs the repository at draft_pr autonomy.

nodes.title: Sign the digest and gather its SBOM

config.brief: Record the published image's name, digest and SBOM for the Transparency Exchange.

name: Deploy failed card
description: When a deployment to production fails, the explainer files a card with the diff since the last good deployment and the failing step, for whoever owns the rollback.

config.brief: Explain the failed deployment named in the trigger: the failing step, the lines that matter, and the diff since the last good deployment to the same environment.
